evidence_type: independent implementation-only source review and retained-test-log inspection
status: reviewed corrections confirmed by inspection; native runtime remains unverified
source_identity: Reviewed working-tree files are individually fingerprinted below; the parent commit alone does not identify the uncommitted shortcut/vendor changes.
scope: Native shortcut manager/callback/registration lifecycle, focused input, rebind/disable/reset, settings acknowledgements, hidden-window recovery/close, related worker settings policy, and narrow eframe hidden-root wake extension.
evaluator_actions: Read source/tests and primary API documentation; compute file/log hashes and inspect retained test outcomes. No implementation edits, Cargo build/test run, native key/window registration, GUI/CUA, keyboard injection, capture, inference or permission change.

defects_corrected.trigger: Pinned global-hotkey macOS unregister fails after its internal native handle has been removed. A later upstream call can return success without cleaning that handle.
defects_corrected.correction: Typed RestartRequired latches the uncertain state, suppresses callbacks, retains cleanup identity, and blocks retry/re-registration/shutdown from converting an upstream no-op into success. Normal data-safe exit remains available.
defects_corrected.verification: Inspected adapter and Manager paths; pointer-loss fake regression preserves the failure, skips later cleanup calls and prevents new registrations. Actual OS cleanup failure was not induced.

defects_corrected.trigger: A delayed raw callback from a retired chord registration arrives after the same deterministic chord ID is reused; bridge queue epochs alone cannot distinguish it.
defects_corrected.correction: Mac IDs increase monotonically; the exact allocated HotKey is retained per action and used for unregister. Checked exhaustion refuses wrap/reuse.
defects_corrected.verification: Inspected native adapter and pure allocation/exhaustion regression, plus fake raw callback rejection after rebind/pause/resume and bounded-queue regression. No native event timing was exercised.

defects_corrected.trigger: Shortcut editing appeared enabled during capture, while the existing whole-settings worker policy rejects those writes.
defects_corrected.correction: Record/reset controls are disabled while capture settings are locked, with explicit stop/wait feedback. Existing registered shortcuts remain active.
defects_corrected.verification: Inspected capture_busy predicate/control gates and semantic disabled-controls regression. Worker/runtime policy was preserved.

defects_corrected.trigger: A root CloseRequested event arrives while every window is hidden and no assistant focus request exists. Skipping App::ui bypassed the CancelClose/data-finalization guard.
defects_corrected.correction: App::logic also requests the one-shot UI pass for close_requested, allowing the existing close guard to run.
defects_corrected.verification: Inspected predicate and actual integration close handling. App regression keeps ROOT/child RawInput identities distinct and asserts CancelClose, no Close, visible assistant and unsaved notes preserved. Vendor EpiIntegration regression checks should_close remains false. No OS Dock/menu close routing was tested.

other_paths_reviewed: The macOS process-wide handler is installed before the one retained native manager; callbacks only enqueue bounded events and wake the root. Manager methods remain on the owning UI thread.
The callback queue has capacity 32; no blocking send, inference, capture or app effects execute in native callbacks.
Per-action epochs invalidate already queued software events; fresh native IDs reject delayed callbacks after re-registration.
Windows one-shot actions use MOD_NOREPEAT, repeatable move/scroll actions allow repeat, IDs are fresh within the documented application range, and failed unregister retains the exact ID for retry.

Focused matching uses exact supported modifiers. Registered chords consume focused input without a second dispatch; repeats do not trigger one-shot actions. Invalid duplicate/reserved bindings use a typed non-dispatching status.

New shortcut defaults/overrides, explicit null disable and reset semantics map to the stable core action IDs. A central pending guard prevents stale whole-settings writes before the prior acknowledgement.
Bare Mac Backspace clears the recorded binding; modified Backspace remains recordable. The revised test supplies the real release/press transition and preserves repeat suppression.

The wake extension consumes a one-shot Frame request and retains the independent wgpu visibility guard. Constructor initialization covers native, web and kittest paths; it does not itself show the hidden root.
Global registration is disabled in fixtures/headless managers. Linux global registration remains explicitly unsupported; focused fallback is separate.

executed_checks_observed.binding_limit: Execution/source association is reported by the owner with functional source held; evaluator fingerprints identify the inspected files and independently bind the retained output, not a fresh-build attestation.
executed_checks_observed.format_and_diff_checks: Desktop owner reported cargo fmt --all --check and owned diff-check passed; evaluator did not execute them.

limits: No real macOS or Windows hotkey API, registration conflict, native event ordering, suspend/resume, cross-application focus, all-hidden wake/quit or OS permission workflow was executed by the evaluator.

Headless fake registrars and actual EpiIntegration tests verify code paths, not native dispatch or reference-product parity. Native child accessibility and measured visual behavior remain separate checks.
The Mac restart-required path deliberately cannot release a handle the pinned library lost; process exit is the recovery boundary. It must not claim cleanup success.
Linux global registration remains unavailable in this build. This review does not establish cross-platform runtime support or release acceptance.
Configured-weight tests were ignored in the ordinary suite. No ASR/generation accuracy or capture-quality claim is made.
The earlier resource-blocked isolated vendor build and both failed headless attempts remain visible. Root owns final registry/progress/STATUS checks and publication.
